key_insight: Gradient-aware AI agents can autonomously discover and train turbulence closures by combining LLM-guided model search with differentiable CFD.
engineering_relevance: This approach could reduce manual closure design and calibration for turbulence simulations, including large-eddy simulation of wall-bounded flows.
method: Use multi-agent LLMs to search analytical, neural, and hybrid closure forms.
Embed proposals in a GPU-native differentiable CFD solver and validate objectives and gradient paths.
Use truncated-horizon gradients for parameter training and feed simulation results back into model search.
evidence_signal: Tests cover 2D dissipation and subgrid-scale closures plus 3D channel-flow wall models; gradient-based training recovers reference coefficients missed by forward evaluation within the same budget and improves targeted reference statistics.
watch_item: Truncated-horizon gradients enable training under chaotic dynamics, but agreement with targeted statistics does not establish generalization to unseen flow conditions.
paper_title: Gradient-Aware AI Agents for Autonomous Turbulence Model Discovery via Differentiable CFD
